history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Gangotri' is approximate. The temple is actually at Bhaironghati, ~10 km from Gangotri on the Gangotri-Uttarkashi road (NH 108), at the confluence of the Jadh Ganga (Jahanvi) and Bhagirathi rivers. Bhairon Nath (Bhairava) is venerated here as the kshetrapal - protector of the Gangotri region; per legend, Shiva chose Bhairon Nath as the region's guardian, and every visit to Gangotri temple should be followed by darshan at Bhairon Nath. The shrine stands amid forests; one source places it across the Jahanvi river, reached on foot beyond Bhaironghati. About 3 km onward is Lanka Chatti, with one of the region's highest river bridges over the Jahanvi. Coordinates are the Bhaironghati settlement (Wikipedia: 31.0097, 78.8793); the map geocoder could not resolve the temple/hamlet precisely - pin is settlement-level (verify). NOTE: do not confuse with the famous Bhairon Temple at Bhairon Ghati near Vaishno Devi (J&K).

name: Bhairon Nath Temple, Bhaironghati
town: Bhaironghati (CSV town 'Gangotri' is approximate; actual location ~10 km from Gangotri)
town_description: Bhaironghati is a small settlement in Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand, at the juncture of the Jadh Ganga (Jahanvi) and Bhagirathi rivers on the Gangotri-Uttarkashi road (NH 108), ~10 km from Gangotri. Reported elevation varies 2,806-3,307 m across sources (verify). It is known for the deep Jadh Ganga gorge beneath the NH 108 girder bridge and as the site of the guardian Bhairon Nath shrine of the Gangotri region.

travel.road: ~10 km from Gangotri on the Gangotri-Uttarkashi road; the shrine across the Jahanvi river is reached on foot (per indiatraveltimes.com)
